papers.abstract: Set-based language model routing aims to increase the coverage of the event where at least one model answers a query correctly while controlling the number of inference calls made.

papers.title: Agent4Spec: An LLM-based Agentic System to Optimize API Specifications through Automated Validation and Market Analysis
papers.abstract: API specifications serve as critical documentation for modern software development, directly impacting integration efficiency and client code generation.

papers.title: OWLET: On-Policy Weighted Learning via Evidence Transfer for Video Large Language Model Post-Training
papers.abstract: Post-training has become a key stage for eliciting reasoning capabilities in Video Large Language Models (Video-LLMs). Existing post-training methods mainly follow two paradigms: reinforcement learning (RL) and on-policy distillation (OPD). However, they do not fully exploit visual evidence for effective training.

papers.title: ConClick: Element-Wise Contrastive Learning Improves GUI Grounding
papers.abstract: GUI grounding, the task of locating the interface element specified by a user instruction, is a fundamental capability of GUI agents. However, existing grounding models remain error-prone, often causing downstream task failures.

papers.title: Forgetting is Not Always Bad: A Neuro-Inspired Memory Repair Mechanism for Poisoned LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are highly vulnerable to memory-poisoning attacks. Existing defenses primarily rely on external modules for either static memory isolation or continuous online auditing, resulting in low memory efficiency and high computational overhead.

papers.title: CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) reveals versatility and convenience during VLM post-training, providing dense supervision for student from teacher. However, we observed an anomaly that the distilled VLM could still answer the questions accurately even when the related visual regions were masked or replaced with noise.

papers.title: SheafPrune: Sheaf-Guided Graph Propagation for Visual Token Pruning
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models process the complete visual token sequence, increasing prefill cost even when many tokens are irrelevant to the instruction. Token-wise saliency captures limited inter-token dependence; graph-based selection instead depends on how relations govern importance propagation and ranking.

papers.title: Dual-Stream Memory for Vision-Language-Action Policies
papers.abstract: Memory-dependent manipulation requires a policy to track execution state and recover visual evidence that is no longer observable. We propose dual-stream memory for vision-language-action policies, assigning these requirements to complementary representations.

papers.title: Data-Adaptive Mahalanobis Metric Learning for Cross-Head Attention in Transformers
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose Data-Adaptive Mahalanobis Cross-Head Attention (DAMCHA), a simple and effective attention mechanism that generalizes Multi-Head Attention (MHA) through the lens of metric learning.

papers.title: Beyond a Single Crop: Contextualized Embeddings for Player Re-Identification
papers.abstract: Person re-identification is typically addressed by learning identity-discriminative embeddings from individual person crops.

papers.title: Neural Surrogate Modeling of Ultrasonic Wave Propagation in Heterogeneous Media
papers.abstract: Neural surrogates provide computationally efficient auto-regressive modeling of wave propagation, enabling e.g. fast inverse solutions. Despite recent progress, the current surrogates are not yet sufficient for the needs of ultrasonic sensing, characterized by high frequency and heterogeneous propagation media.

papers.title: CAST: Credit Alignment for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Cross-tokenizer on-policy distillation (OPD) requires aligning teacher and student sequences before their scores can be compared. Decoded-text alignment provides such correspondence at the chunk level, but leaves a distinct problem unresolved: credit alignment.

papers.title: Tabular Foundation Models Are Effectively Shallow
papers.abstract: In-context-learning Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) are uniquely suited to scenarios with limited resources or privacy constraints, as they solve new tasks without additional training. However, their architecture consists of multiple transformer blocks, resulting in high computational and memory footprints.

papers.title: Vision Transformers Learn Word Meaning from Images Alone
papers.abstract: Can a vision model learn what words mean from pixels alone? We show that the two largest DINOv3 vision transformers organize words rendered in images by word meaning, despite being pretrained using self-supervision on images only, without paired captions, class labels, or other language supervision.

papers.title: What Do Audio-Language Judges of Generated Music Listen For? Four Probes with Controls from Expert Ratings
papers.abstract: Open audio-language models are used as judges of generated music: given a clip and its text prompt, the model rates the clip, and the judge is validated by how well its ratings correlate with expert ratings.

papers.title: Jag: Direct Box Prediction for Efficient Visual Grounding
papers.abstract: Visual grounding combines image--language understanding with geometric prediction, yet autoregressive multimodal models often express a box as a coordinate sequence. Sequential decoding adds computation to the multimodal processing needed for localization.

papers.title: State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents
papers.abstract: On-Policy Distillation (OPD) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for transferring reasoning capabilities from frontier models to smaller models, while extending its success to multi-turn agentic environments remains challenging.

papers.title: The Predictability Bias of Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning in Medical Imaging
papers.abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn by predicting teacher representations of masked regions from visible context. Point prediction summarizes the conditional target distribution and cannot reproduce variation that the context does not resolve. We call this constraint predictability bias.

papers.title: How Reliable are AMR Parser Outputs? Uncertainty Estimation for AMR Parsing
papers.abstract: Recent advances have significantly improved the performance of Abstract Meaning Representation (AMR) parsers, yet determining when their outputs can be trusted remains largely unexplored.

papers.title: Learning Schwarzschild Geodesic Motion with Lagrangian Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Lagrangian Neural Networks (LNNs) learn dynamics from trajectory data by parameterizing a scalar Lagrangian and deriving accelerations through the Euler--Lagrange equation, providing a variational inductive bias that improves physical consistency over purely data-driven models.

papers.title: FPD-Drive: Future Policy Distillation for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving models are typically trained on real-world driving logs, which record only the trajectory actually executed in each scene. This provides limited supervision for learning alternative valid behaviors.

papers.title: ReSFlow: Rectifying Categorical Flows on Statistical Manifolds for One-Step Generation
papers.abstract: Generative modeling for discrete data has been significantly advanced by learning continuous vector fields on the statistical manifolds to transport simple priors to target discrete distributions.

papers.title: Automated Detection and Encoding of Cartographic Signs in Historical Maps
papers.abstract: Symbols and icons in archival maps represent an expansive source of evidence for historical geography. In this paper, we present a two-stage framework for (1) detecting cartographic signs in historical maps and (2) generating interpretable sign embeddings that capture both semantics and stylistic variations.

papers.title: Tensor-based Fusion of Multi-modal Data for Predicting Cancer Risk Levels
papers.abstract: Cancer diagnosis and treatment increasingly rely on multi-modal diagnostic technologies that generate high-dimensional datasets. Although these datasets are rich in pathological information, they pose considerable challenges in interpretation, dimensionality reduction, and clinical applicability.

papers.title: Multi-Modal Graph Neural Network-Inspired Vessel Identification and Tracking for UAV-Based Maritime Surveillance
papers.abstract: The unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based maritime surveillance is becoming an important part of maritime Internet of Things (IoT) and intelligent transportation systems. It provides a flexible and cost-effective way to large-scale maritime traffic monitoring.

papers.title: Complexity-Calibrated Reconstruction Discrepancy for No-Reference Point Cloud Quality Assessment
papers.abstract: The discrepancy induced by surface reconstruction in a distorted point cloud is jointly influenced by its intrinsic structural complexity and signal degradation.

papers.title: Golden Anchor for Video Generation
papers.abstract: Video generation supports digital content creation, with applications in virtual avatars, AI-driven filmmaking, interactive game engines, and world models.

papers.title: Monarch-MoE: Structured Experts for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
papers.abstract: Learning new tasks in multimodal continual instruction tuning can cause catastrophic forgetting of previously acquired knowledge. Although multi-expert LoRA distributes learning across experts, updates to a dense low-rank expert can still affect many output features.

papers.title: Beyond Actions: Learning Future Operation Targets for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Actions specify what a robot should execute, but do not describe what those commands will achieve. Vision-language-action (VLA) policies nevertheless learn primarily by predicting action chunks from images, language, and state.

papers.title: Verifiable Sampling for Delegated Generative Quantum Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Generative machine learning has shown remarkable results across a wide range of interdisciplinary tasks, motivating significant efforts toward Quantum Generative Models as a path to beyond-classical performance, given their capability of generating classically intractable distributions.

papers.title: How Much Computation Does Every Forecast Need? Structured Block Skipping in Two Time-Series Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Time-series foundation models use the same network depth for every input, although forecasting windows differ in structure and difficulty. We test whether whole Transformer blocks can be removed at inference time in two pretrained models: Chronos-Bolt and TimesFM 2.5.

papers.title: SharP: Soft and Hard Prompt-Guided Augmentation with LLM for Low Resource Fake News Detection
papers.abstract: Fake news detection under low resource conditions is challenged by the scarcity of labeled data and the difficulty of capturing subtle deceptive patterns.

papers.title: Rethinking Relative Policy Differences Transfer of On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a target policy on its own rollouts using token-level supervision from a stronger teacher, but typically relies on the teacher being substantially more capable than the target.

papers.title: S$^3$R: Fast and Faithful RL Rollouts via Self-Sparse Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Fast rollout generation for long-context reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) requires reducing KV-cache traffic without changing the response groups used for policy optimization. In our profiled RLVR workloads, attention accounts for 72--76\% of autoregressive decoding kernel time.

papers.title: Does Learning Recurrent Networks Matter in Partially Observable RL?
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) under partial observability typically re- lies on recurrent networks to encode temporal information, with the recurrent module trained jointly with the policy or value function. This raises a natural question: is learning the recurrent network actually necessary?

papers.title: JANUS: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models
papers.abstract: Long-horizon autonomous research has shown promise in accelerating scientific progress through sustained cycles of hypothesis generation, implementation, and validation.

papers.title: Prediction-Informed Landing Window Planning for UAV Landing on USV in High Sea States
papers.abstract: Autonomous landing of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) on unmanned surface vehicle (USV) is difficult in high sea states. Existing hierarchical landing methods often infer future USV motion only implicitly from short observation histories, which limits their ability to adapt to severe and rapidly changing sea conditions.

papers.title: Destination-Conditioned Adaptation with Semantic-Geometric Alignment for Generative Inbetweening
papers.abstract: Generative inbetweening aims to synthesize temporally coherent intermediate frames between a start frame and a target frame. Although pretrained image-to-video diffusion models provide strong priors for large-motion inbetweening, they are not explicitly designed to reach a specified target frame.

papers.title: WaSA: Wavelet Scattering Autoencoders for Unsupervised Offline Detection of Malicious Clients in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without exposing raw data, yet remains vulnerable to malicious clients injecting poisoned datasets.

papers.title: AdaC-GRPO: Towards Mastering Long-Horizon Visual Sudoku Puzzles via Adaptive Curriculum Learning
papers.abstract: While reinforcement learning with verifiable reward (RLVR) enhances reasoning in large language models, its efficacy in long-horizon multimodal tasks remains underexplored.

papers.title: MixTok: Adaptive Visual Tokenization with Global 1D Tokens and Sparse 2D Refinement
papers.abstract: Efficient visual tokenization requires balancing representation compactness with the preservation of fine-grained image content.

papers.title: High-Throughput Generative Video Super-Resolution on a Single Consumer GPU
papers.abstract: Generative video super-resolution (VSR) can recover visually compelling high-frequency detail by leveraging diffusion priors, but iterative sampling and heavy spatio-temporal coupling make practical deployments difficult.

papers.title: CompactSplat: Spatially Adaptive Gaussian Distribution for Feedforward Scene Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Reconstructing 3D scenes from sparse views without per-scene optimization remains highly challenging, especially for recovering accurate geometry and fine textures.

papers.title: Fix the Match, Not the Solver: STITCH -- a Self-Supervised Compatibility Measure for Eroded Visual Puzzles
papers.abstract: Unlike the clean and pixel-aligned complete pieces of standard jigsaw benchmarks, real-world puzzle fragments lose their boundary regions to erosion, destroying the signal that classical compatibility measures (CMs) rely on.

papers.title: PreCoG: Preview-Edit for Efficient Video Correction in Generation-Time
papers.abstract: Iterative text-to-video generation relies on feedback to correct compositional and temporal failures. However, existing methods typically require another full generation run for each correction, repeating computation and potentially disrupting already correct content.

papers.title: RoleWorld: Knowledge Transfer in World Modeling with Functional Role Abstractions
papers.abstract: World models enable large language model (LLM) agents to anticipate action effects and make informed decisions. For generalization, it is desirable for such world models to transfer efficiently to new environments with similar interaction structure and underlying dynamics.

papers.title: PreSTO: Predictive Subtree Prefetching for Fast LLM Power Sampling
papers.abstract: Power sampling improves large language model (LLM) reasoning at test time by sampling from a sharpened version of the base model's distribution.

papers.title: Scaling Agentic Data for Long-Horizon Terminal Intelligence
papers.abstract: Terminal agents are moving beyond local operations toward completing real-world professional tasks. Short trajectories can demonstrate commands and tool calls, but they do not fully show how agents accumulate evidence through exploration, use it to inform judgments, continually adjust strategies based on feedback, and …

papers.title: SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) for search agents often suffers from evidence fabrication, a failure mode where agents bypass external information ($E_{ext}$) and fabricate an incorrect answer.

papers.title: From Glance to Focus: Mitigating Recognition Laziness in MLLMs for Fine-Grained Recognition
papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) generally fall short of expectations in Fine-Grained Visual Recognition (FGVR), although they exhibit promising FGVR foundations, i.e., visual perception and broad category knowledge.

papers.title: Quality, Not Just Outcome: A Structural Scoring Framework for Selecting Coding-Agent Trajectories for Supervised Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Open coding agents are commonly trained through supervised fine-tuning on interaction trajectories whose final patches pass the benchmark test suite.

papers.title: Les Misérables Dialogue: A film-based network representation of social communication
papers.abstract: In this work, we revisit the classic Les Misérables benchmark network from the perspective of social communication.

papers.title: VIGOR: Verifiable Industrial Geometry Optimization and Repair in Scene Programs
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly generate structured layouts and executable scene programs from natural-language instructions.

papers.title: Competence-Aware Orchestration for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) have emerged as a promising paradigm for enhancing complex reasoning through role specialization and collaboration, yet a key challenge remains: how can collaboration be adapted to a backbone's competence on the current query?

papers.title: DP-MIND: Differentially private memory-guided Long context Inference
papers.abstract: LLM-as-a-Service has become a dominant paradigm for accessing large language models without requiring local deployment. However, the process raises severe privacy concerns when user queries may include sensitive or confidential contexts.

papers.title: Looking Ahead and Back: Anticipatory Generative Modeling for Road-Network Trajectories
papers.abstract: Trajectory generation underpins urban applications such as traffic management and urban planning. Within road networks, vehicle movement along road segments is largely deterministic, whereas transitions at intersections are critical--multiple outgoing paths may appear equally plausible, yet they can lead to …

papers.title: Fast Gradient-Based Approximation of Continuous Dynamic Time Warping
papers.abstract: Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) is a common choice for measuring the discrepancy between time series. It proceeds by finding an optimal warping between timestamps through dynamic programming, which can be slow and is not differentiable. Consequently, several variants have been proposed.

papers.title: Locate, Judge, Read: Role-Specialized Tool Agents over a Knowledge-Point Index for Open-Domain Multimodal Document QA
papers.abstract: Question answering over large heterogeneous document collections requires first finding the right passages and then reading them, yet current retrieval-augmented agents give one model both kinds of tools and let it schedule itself.

papers.title: Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality
papers.abstract: A solid understanding of the predictive success of deep neural networks (DNNs) remains elusive. For example, while many data-dependent metrics exist that seek to predict model quality of DNNs, these metrics may be expensive to compute for large datasets and/or may be impossible to compute when training datasets are …

papers.title: GuidedNav: Shaping Vision-Language Navigation Representations through Pre-action Attention and Spatial Guidance
papers.abstract: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) requires an agent to track progress through an extended instruction, identify landmarks relevant to its current objective, and understand the surrounding spatial structure to act.

papers.title: BenCoDiC: A Large-Scale Contextual Cyberbullying Corpus for Bengali Political News Discourse FULL VERSION
papers.abstract: Cyberbullying is a growing concern in online communities, yet existing Bengali corpora remain limited in contextual information, annotation transparency, scale, accessibility, and support for multidimensional analysis, thereby hindering robust detection and comprehensive study of harasser behaviors and networks.

papers.title: Replaying the Movie in Your Mind Decoding Dynamic Visual Perception and Recall from EEG
papers.abstract: Decoding dynamic visual content from EEG has advanced rapidly for visual perception, yet it remains unclear which aspects of neural representations are preserved when people internally replay dynamic scenes.

papers.title: DRYLAB-Bench: Benchmarking the Biosecurity Risk of Agentic LLM Mutation Design
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) acquire advanced biological design capabilities, they offer substantial research benefits but simultaneously introduce severe dual-use risks, such as engineering enhanced pathogens or drug-resistant bacteria.

papers.title: Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation
papers.abstract: Continual post-training faces a dual challenge of acquisition and retention: models must learn new capabilities while preserving prior knowledge.

papers.title: Does Location Matter? A Black-Box Causal Audit Reveals Model-Dependent Audio Grounding in LALM Hallucination
papers.abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) frequently exhibit object hallucination, affirming absent sounds. The dominant mitigation, Audio-Aware Decoding (AAD), contrasts logits under real audio against an all-zero "blank" waveform, flagged by prior review as out-of-distribution.

papers.title: What Do Visual-Head Discovery Scores Actually Find? Attention Source, Necessity, and Random-Control Pitfalls in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Attention heads that attend to image regions relevant to a question are increasingly used to steer, ground and interpret vision-language models (VLMs) and to reduce their hallucinations. They are mostly found by ranking heads with an attention- pattern score and validated by steering or masking them.

papers.title: Scaling RNA Foundation Models through Iterative Refinement
papers.abstract: Biological function in RNA is encoded across scales, from local sequence motifs to long-range structural dependencies. Conventional RNA foundation models couple parameter capacity and inference depth within a fixed architecture, prescribing a fixed computation graph for each inference.

papers.title: Can Failed Trajectories Reveal Where Agents Go Wrong? Agentic Failure Attribution Without Step-Level Labels
papers.abstract: Failure attribution for LLM agents aims to identify decisive steps responsible for task failure, which is critical for debugging and improving agentic systems. Existing methods rely on costly LLM prompting, step-level error annotations, or verified successful trajectories that lack failure signals for assistance.

papers.title: Robust Vision-Language Navigation with Awareness of Instruction-Execution Progress
papers.abstract: In Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) tasks involving multi-step instructions as guidance, an agent must associate its observations with the relevant instruction content at each decision point.

papers.title: From 2.1M Hours of Raw Broadcast Audio to Finnish Speech SSL: Confidence Filtering and Architectural Analysis at Scale
papers.abstract: Broadcast archives offer scale and diversity for self-supervised learning (SSL) but contain substantial noisy, non-speech, and multilingual content. Prior work typically relies on voice activity detection or language identification (LID) to extract speech, ensuring presence rather than quality.

papers.title: VETR: Execution-Grounded Self-Improving Agent for Symbolic Graphics Reasoning
papers.abstract: Visual agents for symbolic graphics reasoning depend on executable world representations, yet continued improvement remains bottlenecked by ambiguous supervision from final renders.

papers.title: Stochastic Finite-Transition Learning and Exploration for Accelerated MRI Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Generative MRI reconstruction maps an initial source distribution to the target image distribution along a learned recovery trajectory.

papers.title: When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows
papers.abstract: AI agents depend on repeated decisions to accomplish tasks, with large language models (LLMs) commonly serving as their core decision makers. The recent emergence of Jev offers an opportunity to make these decisions faster and at lower cost.

papers.title: Volume Rendering with Metric--Phase Fields for Thin Structures and Sign-Ambiguous Geometry
papers.abstract: Neural implicit surface methods that couple volume rendering with signed distance functions (SDFs), such as VolSDF and NeuS, achieve high-quality multi-view reconstruction for watertight objects. However, these approaches rely on a globally consistent inside-outside partition of space.

papers.title: The Limits of Query Monitoring against Distributed Model Extraction
papers.abstract: Model providers now face distillation campaigns run through thousands of accounts, each of which looks like an ordinary user. When network and payment metadata cannot link those accounts, the only evidence left is what they ask.

papers.title: Human and LLM Facilitation in Collaborative Design Meetings: A Computational Behavioral Comparison
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored as facilitators of group discussion and collaborative work, but the behavioral differences between LLM-generated and human facilitation remain insufficiently characterized.

papers.title: SWEAR: Section-Wise Efficient Audio Reasoning via Self-Rated Difficulty
papers.abstract: Recent work on large audio-language models (LALMs) explores adaptive reasoning to balance accuracy and efficiency. However, existing approaches often rely on coarse-grained difficulty estimation, overlooking the diverse factors that determine reasoning effort.

papers.title: Attention Sees, MLP Refuses: Tracing the Attention-to-MLP Safety Pathway in LLMs
papers.abstract: Safety-aligned large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to jailbreaks and can over-refuse benign requests. Understanding these failures requires distinguishing harmfulness recognition from the computation that writes refusal.

papers.title: LongHarness: Advancing Agentic Reasoning over 100M-Token Corpora via Stateful Evidence Management
papers.abstract: Corpus-level long-context reasoning requires agents to acquire and integrate evidence across document collections that exceed their context windows.

papers.title: Double-Take: Improving Capacity, Binding, and Selectivity In Long-Context Within Bidirectional Memory
papers.abstract: Processing a long sequence does not guarantee that distant information remains usable. As context grows, a fixed-size memory must retain many associations, connect information across positions, and preserve relevant structure without being overwhelmed by everything it observes.

papers.title: AV-FlowEdit: Training-Free Prompt-Driven Audio-Visual Editing with Event-Aware Spectral Trajectory Preservation
papers.abstract: Joint audio-video diffusion models generate synchronized content, but editing existing clips requires target changes without disrupting non-target structure or cross-modal correspondence. We present AV-FlowEdit, a training-free and inversion-free framework for prompt-driven audio-video editing.

papers.title: Evolving Creatives with Clicks: CTR-Driven Advertising image Editing via Attribute Disentanglement and Preference Alignment
papers.abstract: The optimization objective for e-commerce advertising creatives has shifted from aesthetic quality to online business metrics like click-through rate (CTR).

papers.title: CB-Orchestrator: Adaptive Workflow Optimization for LLM Agents via Contextual Bandits
papers.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in tackling complex tasks through agentic workflows. However, manually designing these workflows is labor-intensive and lacks flexibility to adapt to diverse queries.

papers.title: KV-Repurpose: A Testbed for Evaluating Non-Prefix KV-Cache Reuse
papers.abstract: KV-cache reuse in large language model serving is commonly limited to exact prompt prefixes, preventing reuse when the same retrieved document appears after different system prompts, conversation histories, or dynamic metadata.

papers.title: CliQ-RRG: Clinical-Knowledge Guided Disease-aware Visual-Textual Alignment for QA-Style Radiology Report Generation
papers.abstract: Radiology reports are essential for diagnostic reasoning and patient care, yet their manual preparation is time-consuming and cognitively demanding.

papers.title: Travel Back To Move Forward: Retrospective Exploration and Evolving for Long Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: Large language model agents increasingly operate in long-horizon environments where early mistakes can trigger cascading failures and trap agents in dead-end trajectories. Agents must therefore be able to proactively recover from such states and turn their exploratory experience into guidance for subsequent decisions.

papers.title: CoBe: A Benchmark For Conversational Counterfactual Text Editing
papers.abstract: Counterfactual text editing is the ability to revise a given text in light of a hypothetical change while preserving facts not causally affected by that change.

papers.title: A4-MR: Abnormality-aware Anatomical Alignment for MR
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large-scale foundation models have enabled strong generalization across a wide range of clinical and research tasks in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

papers.title: UniMergeTrack: Hierarchical Model Merging for General RGB-X Visual Object Tracking
papers.abstract: RGB-X tracking leverages complementary modalities, such as thermal infrared, event, or depth, to improve robustness under challenging conditions. Existing general-purpose RGB-X trackers typically follow two paradigms: independent task-specific training and joint training across modality combinations.

papers.title: Space Over Statistic, Retraining Over Ranking: Auditing Training Labels Under Label-Only Backdoors
papers.abstract: Some backdoor attacks never touch an image. FLIP only changes labels: on CIFAR-10, flipping 3% of them makes a ResNet-32 send 99.7% of triggered source-class images to the attacker's class. The usual defenses look for the poison inside a model trained on those same labels.

papers.title: NOFACE3D: NOise-scheduled Focused Anchoring and Controlled Enhancement for 3D Generation
papers.abstract: Recent image-to-3D models generate complete, high-quality assets from a single image, with global shape and appearance that are already convincing; what remains is the fine scale, where small, thin, elongated, or detail-rich regions are reconstructed softly and under-resolved.

papers.title: Redirecting Teacher Supervision: Temporal-Response-Guided Latent Distillation for Video-Language Models
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers capabilities through teacher predictions on student-generated sequences, as studied by GKD and MiniLLM for language models and Video-OPD for video tasks. We ask how internal supervision can further support temporal learning.

papers.title: RAMP: Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision for Efficient Prefill in Recurrent-Depth Language Models
papers.abstract: Recurrent-depth language models improve inference-time reasoning by repeatedly applying a shared network to refine internal representations, but the additional recurrent computation also increases inference cost.

papers.title: Lightweight Time-Frequency Vibration Sensing for Consumer Device Condition Monitoring
papers.abstract: Consumer rotating devices, including washing machines, air conditioners, electric fans, robotic vacuum cleaners, and home fitness equipment, increasingly rely on vibration sensing for intelligent condition monitoring and predictive maintenance.

papers.title: Towards Easier-to-Tune Training Algorithms: New Results from AlgoPerf
papers.abstract: Evaluating deep learning optimizer is challenging because confounding factors such as hyperparameter tuning and optimizer-model co-design often obscure true algorithmic performance.

papers.title: GeoGR: Spatial-Semantic Token Compression and Group Routing for Efficient 3D VLMs
papers.abstract: Multi-view representations enable pretrained image and video vision-language models to understand 3D scenes, but their long visual token sequences make inference costly.

papers.title: Target-Constrained Pooling for Trajectory Extrapolation
papers.abstract: Trajectory extrapolation from a partial target trajectory is underdetermined, but completed related trajectories provide information about the unresolved continuation.

papers.title: Low-Rank Kolmogorov-Arnold Generator Flows for Interpretable Operator Learning
papers.abstract: Neural operators that learn physical laws from data should generalize beyond their training distribution and expose the learned law in closed form.

papers.title: Dataset-Specific Encoding of Image Content Underlies Cross-Dataset Failure in Brain MRI Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Frozen features of brain MRI foundation models lose accuracy on new datasets, a failure usually blamed on the features encoding where each scan came from. We show that the failure lies elsewhere.

papers.title: Evo$^2$: Evolving the Evolver through Weight-Harness Co-Evolution
papers.abstract: Self-evolving agents are increasingly used to improve language model systems without human intervention through either weight updates or harness improvements.

papers.title: What Visual Representations Do World Action Models Need?
papers.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) inherit powerful priors from pretrained video generation models, but their variational autoencoder (VAE) representations are optimized for visual reconstruction rather than manipulation.

papers.title: Unified Generative Video Compression with Autoregressive and Bidirectional Video Diffusion
papers.abstract: Video diffusion models can reconstruct visually compelling content from severely compressed representations at ultra-low bitrates, but they impose a rigid deployment trade-off.

papers.title: Don't Guess, Just Ask: Evaluating Interactive Requirement Clarification for Repository-Level Software Development
papers.abstract: As LLMs become increasingly capable of implementing software, a critical bottleneck emerges: whether they truly understand what users want. Users often begin with vague intent, leaving important requirements to be clarified through interaction.

papers.title: EmbodiedCLBench: Evaluating Continual Learning for Self-Evolving Embodied Agents
papers.abstract: Continual learning requires models to accumulate past experience and transfer it to new tasks. Despite substantial research on continual learning, existing work remains largely confined to non-embodied settings, without extending to embodied environments.

papers.title: Trajectory-Aware Policy Optimization: Closing the State Distribution Gap in Long-Horizon LLM RL
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a dominant paradigm for enhancing LLMs' reasoning capabilities. Yet long-horizon autoregressive rollouts introduce a fundamental limitation: local policy mismatch can compound into severe state distribution shift over trajectories.

papers.title: FlyHack: Stress-Testing Mechanistic Claims in a Connectome-Constrained Visual Model
papers.abstract: Connectome-constrained neural networks make biological components directly accessible to intervention, but their mechanistic conclusions can still depend on the comparison model, intervention, circuit representation and trained solution.

papers.title: Generalized Proximal Policy Optimization: Unifying LLM RL Algorithms from the Perspective of Divergence
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning has become the foundational paradigm for enhancing the reasoning capabilities of LLMs.

papers.title: Evidential Multimodal Transformers with Dempster-Shafer Fusion for Emotion Recognition
papers.abstract: Softmax-based multimodal emotion recognition methods often assign high confidence even when sensor data are corrupted or contradictory, for example when facial expressions suggest positive valence while vocal prosody indicates negative arousal.

papers.title: Learning Features, Not Layouts: Feature-Axis Attention as a Transfer Prior for Medical Imaging
papers.abstract: Natural-image-pretrained foundation models are increasingly adapted to medical imaging, yet transfer remains unreliable under domain shift, modality heterogeneity, and label scarcity. We trace part of this fragility to an overlooked design choice.

papers.title: Provenance-Aware Belief Updating in Human-AI Feedback Loops
papers.abstract: In repeated human-AI interaction, a single observation can be quoted, summarized, and returned to a model as multiple reports, making repetition look like independent corroboration. We study whether language models can use supplied report lineage to update according to evidence provenance rather than report count.

papers.title: Scaling Empowered Agents
papers.abstract: Empowerment measures the capacity of an agent to actively control its environment. In this work, we explain the connection between skill learning and empowerment.

papers.title: Hindsight Structured Advice Distillation: Steering Executor Agents with Advisors Trained on Their Failures and Task Characteristics
papers.abstract: Language-model agents are used for specialized work such as financial research, healthcare and law. Such agents are often capable enough for a task but still miss its details. In finance, for example, these details include which filing reports a figure or how a company discloses a metric.

papers.title: Evaluating LLM Creativity through Long-Tail Performance
papers.abstract: Creativity benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) vary widely in task and metric design. This raises the question of whether they capture a common notion of creativity.

papers.title: Benchmarking Embedding Geometries and Clustering Algorithms for Unsupervised Patent Claim Classification
papers.abstract: Prior-art retrieval systems are structurally organized around classification codes, making cross-code discovery difficult. This paper asks if an unsupervised representation trained on patent text can recover relevant connections that code-restricted search cannot, and if hyperbolic space helps.

papers.title: What Should SFT Learn? Conditional Information Gain for Generalizable Post-Training
papers.abstract: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) remains a widely used approach for post-training large language models, because fixed demonstrations can directly introduce desired reasoning strategies and behavioral patterns.

papers.title: Language Models Have Interpretable Narrative Mechanisms
papers.abstract: We investigate whether language models contain internal components that contribute to representing narrativity, the degree to which a text exhibits narrative properties.

papers.title: Forecasting Corpus-Sampling Disagreement in Masked Text Reconstruction
papers.abstract: If a second text corpus were collected from the same population, how much would a predictor's outputs change? We study this question for masked-text reconstruction using a smoothed predictor built from nearby token-pair counts and evaluated over the full 50,257-token GPT-2 vocabulary.

papers.title: Scan-Parallel Variational Inference for event-driven Latent Jump Models
papers.abstract: Continuous-time latent state-space models are widely used for irregularly observed time series, typically representing uncertainty through a random initial state followed by smooth ordinary differential equation (ODE) dynamics, or Brownian perturbations accumulated by a stochastic differential equation (SDE).

papers.title: NucleoNet: A Nuclear-Aware Determinant Ansatz for Multi-Geometry Neural Variational Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: Neural-network variational Monte Carlo provides an accurate route to solving the electronic Schrödinger equation, but many neural wavefunctions are optimized for a single nuclear geometry, requiring separate calculations to map out a potential energy surface.

papers.title: Work2Skill: Capturing Human GUI Experience for Reusable Agent Skill Induction
papers.abstract: Computer-use agents can perform increasingly complex GUI tasks, yet unfamiliar software and workflows requiring human domain knowledge remain challenging.

papers.title: The Evidence Anchoring Boundary: Where Visual Interventions Matter and When They Help in Multimodal LLMs
papers.abstract: Visual interventions provide a training-free way to reduce hallucinations in multimodal large language models. However, an intervention may have little leverage at some layers and may damage a correct answer even when it changes the output.

papers.title: Learning Representations to Guide Pixel Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract: Visual representations are largely developed for understanding, yet what makes them useful for generation remains unclear. We study this question in pixel diffusion transformers and uncover two key insights.

papers.title: Beyond Semantic IDs: Finite-Beam Reachability and Continuous-Query Generation in Generative Recommendation
papers.abstract: Generative recommendation (GR) of social media platforms commonly retrieves items by autoregressively decoding discrete Semantic IDs (SIDs) with finite-width beam search.

papers.title: Diffusion Precipitation Generation with Medium-range Weather Forecasting
papers.abstract: Accurate daily precipitation forecasts are important for weather-sensitive decisions. Although recent Weather Foundation Models (WFMs) have achieved significant progress, they are trained on reanalysis data, which exhibit regional and intensity-dependent biases.

papers.title: SmartSalesBench: A Resistance-Aware Multi-Turn Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Sales Agents
papers.abstract: We present SmartSalesBench, the first multi-turn conversational benchmark explicitly designed to evaluate large language model (LLM) sales agents against psychologically grounded, resistant buyer personas.

papers.title: Minions: A Dynamic and Distributed Virtual GPU Cloud Built on Idle Apple Silicon Devices
papers.abstract: The increasing demand for GPU-accelerated machine learning inference has exposed limitations in centralized GPU infrastructures, including high cost, limited elasticity, and long wait times under resource constraints.

papers.title: MotionCoach: Constructing Multimodal Guidance for Video Professional Motion Editing
papers.abstract: Video editing models achieve strong performance in modifying appearance, backgrounds, styles, and motions, empowered by large-scale training data. Beyond general scenarios, professional motions are significant in performance, sports, and martial arts.

papers.title: MVGraph: Benchmarking LVLMs on Evidence Composition across Multi-View Visual Graph
papers.abstract: We introduce MVGraph, a benchmark for evaluating large vision-language models (LVLMs) on multi-graph reasoning where the evidence required by a query is distributed across multiple interrelated visual graph views.

papers.title: DataCupid: Stable Matching Repair for Training Data Acquisition with Delayed Feedback
papers.abstract: Matching repair after utility changes can reuse valid observations, but new evaluations must respect matching capacity and may return out of order. We study announced invalidations with bounded, possibly reward-dependent reporting delays and pending evaluations that do not occupy future matching capacity.

papers.title: Video Codec-Guided Training-Free Token Compression for Video Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Video large language models (VLLMs) rely on long visual token sequences to understand complex temporal content, which makes visual token compression important for efficient inference.

papers.title: JoyInside-VLM-Agent: Product-Conditioned Multimodal Policy Learning for Embodied Agents
papers.abstract: Embodied agents must translate multimodal observations and user requests into executable actions while adapting to product constraints, changing goals, and execution feedback.

papers.title: MathVis: Can AI Reason through Drawing? A Benchmark for Mathematical Figure Generation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces MathVis, a benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to visualize frontier mathematical problems and perform diagram-assisted reasoning.

papers.title: WaveMark: Robust Wavelet-Domain Image Watermarking for Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: Image watermarking enables provenance tracing for photorealistic images generated by diffusion models. However, state-of-the-art (SOTA) removal attacks can suppress embedded signals with little perceptual degradation.

papers.title: From Imbalance to Evidence: Deep Nonparametric Testing for Complex Data under Severe Sample Imbalance
papers.abstract: Comparing distributions under severe sample imbalance requires effectively using abundant majority observations while retaining sensitivity to differences involving the smaller sample.

papers.title: In-Context Learning Can Help Vision-Language Models Overcome Training Priors
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) learn strong statistical regularities during training, which can make them fail to properly respond to visual evidence when input images violate those regularities.

papers.title: UniDeblur: Unified Motion Deblurring via Fourier Convolution Learning
papers.abstract: Image deblurring is a fundamental task in computer vision, yet existing methods mainly specialize in isolated scenarios. Consequently, the deblurring performance of these models drops significantly across scenarios with different cameras and image contents.

papers.title: Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training
papers.abstract: Large language models have achieved remarkable advances in complex reasoning. However, scaling reasoning post-training with ever-larger corpora can substantially increase training cost without proportional performance gains.

papers.title: SEEDS: Preview-Guided Evidence Admission for Search Agents
papers.abstract: Search agents extend large reasoning models with multi-round access to external knowledge, yet most existing systems largely conflate retrieving evidence with consuming it.

papers.title: Collaborative Learning and Reasoning over Model Slices
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) excel across diverse tasks, benefiting from knowledge priors, in-context reasoning, and test-time computation.

papers.title: What Egocentric Video Embeddings Encode and How to Combine Them with Inertial Sensors for Human Activity Recognition
papers.abstract: Egocentric video and body-worn inertial sensors are increasingly recorded together, and the video is usually encoded by pretrained models. What these embeddings represent when the camera sits on the head, and how they should be combined with inertial sensing, has received little attention.

papers.title: Sparse Dictionary Learning for Measure-Valued Data via Linearized Optimal Transport: Efficient Algorithms and Sample Complexity
papers.abstract: We study dictionary learning for probability measure-valued data by embedding measures into Hilbert spaces using features derived from optimal transport geometry.

papers.title: Teaching neural decoders with language
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces decode neural activity, yet class-label supervision (CLS) leaves relationships among classes implicit.

papers.title: Beyond Second-Order Information: Paid Logistic Regression with Noisy Features
papers.abstract: We consider online binary prediction with paid stochastic features, where the learner can spend resources to obtain better observations of the underlying features.

papers.title: AI-Mediation in Retail Markets: Revenue Effects and Assortment Optimization
papers.abstract: AI shopping assistants increasingly influence which products consumers consider. We study retail assortment planning under AI mediation, where a retailer chooses a catalog, an AI intermediary forms a customer-facing shortlist, and the customer chooses from that shortlist according to a multinomial logit model.

papers.title: DeFiRank: Federated Pairwise Ranking for Governance in Decentralized Financial Networks
papers.abstract: Existing governance approaches in decentralized financial networks rely on manual review processes conducted by human committees, which introduces subjective bias, creates a scalability bottleneck under high network volume, and fails to capture complex behavioural patterns and evolving network dynamics.

papers.title: Controlled-Minimax: Stabilizing Adversarial Optimization via Control Theory
papers.abstract: Minimax optimization is fundamental to adversarial learning yet suffers from severe stability challenges, often manifesting as persistent limit cycles or divergence. This paper investigates these instabilities through the lens of continuous-time dynamical systems.

papers.title: OGPO: Offline Goal-conditioned Policy Optimization for Recoverable Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown strong promise in robotic manipulation, yet their post-training still predominantly relies on trajectory-level supervised imitation over robot demonstrations.

papers.title: BLEND: Balancing Personalization vs. Generalization in Federated Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Federated vision-language models (FedVLMs) represent one of the emerging frontiers of machine learning, aiming to integrate federated learning within the fine-tuning pipelines of vision-language models (VLMs).

papers.title: GIST: Generator-state-Informed Supervision for Tabular Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) based on prior-data fitted networks typically use sampled hard query labels, leaving avoidable sampling variability in pretraining. A key observation is that intermediate generator states can reveal label uncertainty beyond a sampled outcome.

papers.title: JMT-YOLO: Multi-task Domain Adaptation via Segmentation-Guided Consistency Learning
papers.abstract: Domain adaptive object detection (DAOD) aims to reduce performance degradation due to distribution shifts between training (source) and testing (target) datasets.

papers.title: A Lightweight Velocity Correction Framework for Improving Instruction Following in Few-Step Text-to-Image Generation
papers.abstract: Few-step text-to-image generators produce high-quality images with few network forward passes, yet struggle with complex prompts involving multiple subjects, interactions, spatial relations, counting, and attribute binding.

papers.title: Rethinking the Roles of Diffusion and Decoding: Predictive-State Flows for Parallel Language Generation
papers.abstract: In continuous diffusion language models (DLMs), latents generated by the diffusion prior are mapped almost deterministically to tokens, either by a decoder or through a token embedding matrix.

papers.title: AD-SRF: Attack-Defense Semantic Reinforcement for Multi-Modal Image Fusion
papers.abstract: Existing image fusion methods struggle to balance visual quality and semantic attributes due to the inherent conflict between their optimization objectives. To address this challenge, we propose an attack-defense semantic reinforcement framework for multi-modal image fusion, termed AD-SRF.

papers.title: MeshBind: Point-to-Mesh Binding for Non-Rigid Scene Flow Automatic Annotation
papers.abstract: Scene flow estimation is essential for many autonomous driving (AD) and robotic applications, but obtaining ground-truth scene flow for non-rigid objects such as pedestrians is highly difficult.

papers.title: Generalized Determinantal Point Processes for Attraction and Repulsion with Distinct Interaction Kernels
papers.abstract: Determinantal point processes (DPPs) model subset selection probability with repulsion, but many applications also exhibit attraction arising from pairwise relations or shared latent structures. Nonsymmetric DPPs (NDPPs) capture both effects, but their kernels are difficult to interpret and specify.

papers.title: Win-Win Fusion: Multi-Modal Image Fusion with Visual-Semantic Collaboration
papers.abstract: Existing multi-modal image fusion (MMIF) methods generally face an optimization gap between the visual and semantic domains, limiting the enhancement of perception capabilities. To overcome this long-standing barrier, this work proposes W2F, a new visual-semantic mutual reinforcing paradigm for MMIF.

papers.title: Personalized Federated Direct Preference Optimization via LoRA Adapters
papers.abstract: Federated Direct Preference Optimization (FedDPO) enables privacy-preserving alignment of language models across distributed agents without centralizing sensitive preference data.

papers.title: CoGameReg: Cooperative-Game-Based Collaborative Semi-Supervised Regression for Seismic Reservoir Property Prediction
papers.abstract: Accurate estimation of reservoir properties from seismic data remains challenging when well-log labels are sparse but three-dimensional seismic observations are abundant.

papers.title: HART: Hybrid Attention-RWKV Time series Foundation Model
papers.abstract: Non-autoregressive multi-step forecasting (NAF) enables time series foundation models to predict an entire future horizon in a single forward pass. Despite its strong sequence modeling capabilities, RWKV-7 exhibits long-horizon degradation in our NAF experiments.

papers.title: Mind the Spatial Gap: A Benchmark for Geospatial Reasoning and Constrained Spatial Editing
papers.abstract: Understanding and manipulating spatial relations is fundamental to AI systems that reason about physical environments and construct grounded world models.

papers.title: One-Step Text Generation by Seq-Drifting
papers.abstract: Diffusion language models generate tokens in parallel, but still require multiple sampling steps to produce high-quality text. In this paper, we investigate whether a model can learn to generate an entire sequence in a single forward pass.

papers.title: When Solvers Get Moody: Quantifying and Predicting Performance Variability in Mixed Integer Programming
papers.abstract: Mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers are widely used, yet their performance can vary substantially even under seemingly neutral perturbations. Such variability complicates benchmarking, and the interpretation of computational studies.

papers.title: Temporal Evidence Forests for Long-Horizon Multi-Party Conversational Memory
papers.abstract: Long-term memory has been widely adopted in LLM-based agents to support persistent interaction and personalized assistance. Long-term multi-party interactions, however, accumulate substantially more detailed information, with decisions repeatedly updated and states evolving across participants and interaction stages.

papers.title: Collaborative Theory of Mind: Learning to Self-Revise by Anticipating User Responses
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong individual task performance, yet still struggle to collaborate with users over extended, multi-turn interactions, for example by attempting solutions before understanding the user's needs or by failing to revise mistaken assumptions after receiving feedback.

papers.title: ROSETTA: Rotation Subspace Estimation for Training-free Transmodal Alignment
papers.abstract: When a query must be matched against a database built with a different sensor or processed by a different encoder, the independently trained encoders impose distinct coordinate systems on the feature space.

papers.title: Localized Generative Design of Ship Hulls with Diffusion Models and High-Fidelity Assessment
papers.abstract: Practical ship design requires localized refinement and performance evaluation. This paper presents a reward-directed diffusion framework for localized hull optimization.

papers.title: Selective Spatio-Temporal Fruit Inspector (S$^2$FI): A Mamba-based Framework for Rotational Fruit Quality Assessment
papers.abstract: The global fruit and vegetable industry confronts severe post-harvest sorting challenges for small and medium-scale growers. Large intelligent sorting systems are too costly, while manual sorting suffers from low efficiency, inconsistent standards, and high labor demand.

papers.title: CaptchaAgent: Verifiable Visual Reasoning for CAPTCHA Solving
papers.abstract: Modern reasoning CAPTCHAs require fine-grained perception, compositional relation reasoning, and grounded browser interaction. End-to-end vision-language model agents remain brittle in this setting because a missed object, incorrect count, or confused relation can propagate directly to the final action.

papers.title: Robust Langevin Sampling under State-Dependent Heavy-Tailed Noise with Applications to LLM Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Existing convergence guarantees for non-log-concave sampling with stochastic gradient Langevin Monte Carlo (SG-LMC) typically assume globally Lipschitz gradients and uniformly bounded noise variance.

papers.title: Time Delay System for Sequence Modeling
papers.abstract: Existing sequence models share a critical limitation: they lack an explicit, interpretable mechanism for content-aware temporal recall. LSTMs compress everything into a single hidden state, thereby losing information about specific past events.

papers.title: Unreliable Narrator Framing as a Cost-effective Mechanism for Satire Explanation of Australian and American Satirical News
papers.abstract: Satirical news is a unique form of misinformation: it is intended to be humorous by the original publication source but can be misinterpreted. Explanation of satirical news articles is challenging because recent and local context needs to be incorporated.

papers.title: Mitigating Capability Degradation in LLM Self-Improvement via Representation Geometry Regularization
papers.abstract: On-Policy Self-distillation is a self-improvement paradigm that enables large language models (LLMs) to improve their capabilities by leveraging the same model as both teacher and student under different conditioning contexts.

papers.title: Universal Bounds for Self-Normalized Kullback-Leibler Estimation
papers.abstract: This work studies an entropy-based estimator of Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence constructed from normalized importance weights. We prove a universal finite-sample bound showing that its expectation can exceed the target-proposal KL divergence by at most $\log 2$ for any sample size.

papers.title: Two-way Guidance: Simultaneous Learning of Summary Statistics for Generative Bayes
papers.abstract: Bayesian simulation-based inference (SBI) can struggle to recover increasingly concentrated posteriors as observation size grows. We consider learning sufficient summary statistics jointly with the posterior as a general principle for scalable inference in various SBI methods.

papers.title: Co-Modifying Application Code and Deployment Infrastructure: A Causal Study of AI Agent Pull Requests
papers.abstract: Current software engineering agents are evaluated predominantly inside isolated sandboxes against synchronous local tests. However, deploying features in collaborative repositories requires modifying continuous integration (CI/CD) pipelines, containers, and provisioning manifests alongside application logic.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning via Fixed-point Flow Matching
papers.abstract: In maximum entropy and behavior-constrained reinforcement learning (RL), the optimal policy is given by a Boltzmann distribution. Generating samples from this distribution can be challenging, as it is often complex and multimodal.

papers.title: Towards Defining, Measuring, and Leveraging Creativity in AI Applications
papers.abstract: Despite extensive research, computational creativity still lacks a conceptually grounded, practically relevant, and empirically applicable formal definition across contexts such as art, scientific research, and games.

papers.title: APEX: Asynchronous Prefix Denoising for Extreme Compression
papers.abstract: Fewer latent tokens promise cheaper diffusion. Yet aggressive latent compression creates a reconstruction-generation dilemma: adding channels improves reconstruction but makes generation harder.

papers.title: Neural networks are more modular than single neurons suggest
papers.abstract: Neural networks routinely develop representations in which individual neurons contribute to multiple distinct functions, leading to the widespread view that such networks lack modular organization.

papers.title: Fear Is Not Always Fear: Variation in Emotion Label Equivalence Across Datasets
papers.abstract: Emotion classifiers are routinely applied beyond their training data, on the assumption that same-named labels such as fear or surprise mean the same thing across resources.

papers.title: COFFEQA: Counterfactual-Guided Few-Shot Distillation for LLM Question Answering
papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation aims to train a smaller student model to mimic a larger teacher model for resource-constrained environments. However, the process of distillation is typically data-intensive and computationally expensive, particularly for generative tasks.

papers.title: Structure-Aware Matching for Robust UAV Thermal-to-Satellite Geo-Localization
papers.abstract: UAV thermal-to-satellite geo-localization localizes UAVs by matching real-time thermal images against georeferenced satellite images, enabling autonomous navigation in GNSS-denied and low-visibility conditions.

papers.title: Cross-Behavior Policy Optimization: Unified Learning from Offline Demonstrations and On- and Off-Policy Rollouts via a Shared Regression Target
papers.abstract: Reasoning post-training draws on offline demonstrations and policy-generated rollouts, yet conventional supervised fine-tuning (SFT) followed by reinforcement learning (RL) separates their objectives and limits continued reuse of collected responses.

papers.title: Scalable Learning of Determinantal Point Processes with Kernel-Structured Interactions
papers.abstract: Determinantal point processes (DPPs) on a finite set are probability models that exhibit repulsion where inter-item similarities are encoded by a positive definite kernel matrix.

papers.title: TreeHCA: Hindsight-Guided Exploration and Credit Assignment for Multi-Turn LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Outcome-supervised group-relative policy optimization (GRPO) assigns the same advantage to every token in an LLM agent trajectory, leaving useful and unhelpful decisions undifferentiated.

papers.title: When Charts Deceive Web Agents: A Paired Benchmark for Misleading Visualization-Grounded Tasks
papers.abstract: Web agents increasingly browse, interpret, and act on web content on behalf of users. In many realistic workflows, however, the visual evidence they consume is not neutral: charts and dashboards can be misleading, shaping judgments without issuing any explicit malicious instruction.

papers.title: Reward Hacking as a Transmissible Strategy in Multi-Agent Coding Systems
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems are increasingly used to solve coding tasks by coordinating agents that share code and plans. These agents are often optimized with reinforcement learning (RL) using automated evaluators, but bypassing evaluation can earn reward without producing a genuine solution.

papers.title: Inverse Synthesis of Shock Time Series from Shock Response Spectra Using Ensembles of Conditional Variational Autoencoders
papers.abstract: The shock response spectrum (SRS) characterizes the peak responses of single-degree-of-freedom systems to transient acceleration. Because the mapping from an acceleration time series (waveform) to its SRS is many-to-one, inverse synthesis seeks candidate waveforms consistent with a prescribed spectrum.

papers.title: LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs
papers.abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn compact latent world models without pixel reconstruction. Existing JEPA pipelines typically train visual representations and action-conditioned dynamics before adding a control policy or solver.

papers.title: Deploying RDMA for Large-Scale Inference and Training Workloads
papers.abstract: RDMA can reduce communication overhead in distributed machine learning systems, but realizing these benefits in production requires more than replacing TCP. Variable-size messages, concurrent connections, bursty incasts, and service failures introduce challenges that hardware offload alone cannot address.

papers.title: VEPA: Verified Evolving Formal Policy for Lifelong LLM Agent Guardrails
papers.abstract: LLM agents increasingly operate over sensitive resources, such as private documents and mutable system states, which can create serious safety and security risks.

papers.title: Spend Where It Matters: Particle Search with MH Refinement for Budget-Constrained Audio-Visual Alignment
papers.abstract: Reward-guided inference-time alignment can improve joint audio-visual generation, but optimizing multiple alignment objectives requires many expensive model evaluations, making existing methods costly under limited compute.

papers.title: The Expressive Power of Random-Feature MPNNs Across Graph Sizes
papers.abstract: Continuous random node features increase the expressivity of message-passing neural networks (MPNNs), but existing theoretical analyses are not fine-grained enough to capture their limitations, particularly in approximating functions across graph sizes or under a fixed number of random bits.

papers.title: Trainable Quantum-Native Language Models: Dissipative Memory, Capacity Limits, and Hardware Validation
papers.abstract: We study byte-level autoregressive language models whose hidden state is a small quantum register, whose transitions are learned token-conditioned quantum channels, and whose next-byte probabilities come directly from Born-rule measurements without a learned classical vocabulary projection or softmax.

papers.title: People Making Conversation: Evaluating How Naturally Speech Models Converse
papers.abstract: A conversational speech model has to decide, at every pause, whether to speak. Existing evaluations test boundary detection, policy adherence, or aggregate statistics, not this decision.

papers.title: Polyconvex neural-network surrogates with learned paired directional features for anisotropic hyperelastic homogenization
papers.abstract: Approximating the effective anisotropic hyperelastic response of a representative volume element (RVE) requires constitutive expressiveness, mechanical consistency, and computational efficiency.

papers.title: Efficient Audio-Visual Speech Enhancement via Reinforcement Learning-Based Neural Architecture Search
papers.abstract: Audio-visual speech enhancement (AVSE) improves speech intelligibility in noisy environments but often relies on computationally expensive models unsuitable for resource-constrained edge devices.

papers.title: Meta-Reflective Evolution Effectively Improves Production AI Systems
papers.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-guided evolutionary optimization has successfully improved prompts, programs, and even entire AI systems. Most optimization methods select a candidate from the search frontier, then mutate it in one LLM pass based only on its failures.

papers.title: Large Language Models, Machine-Assisted Cultural Analytics, and the Agentic Turn
papers.abstract: Technologies like large language models make it easier to convert cultural material into analyzable variables, while LLM-driven agentic systems extend machine assistance to other parts of the research workflow.

papers.title: EvoBelief: Falsifiable World Models for Self-Improving LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Self-evolving LLM agents typically improve how they act through accumulated experience, reflection, or skills. Yet even procedurally capable agents can fail when their beliefs about environment dynamics are incomplete, incorrect, or outdated.

papers.title: Domain Adaptation of SAM 2.1 for Building-Component Segmentation in Image-Based 3D Reconstruction
papers.abstract: 3D reconstruction of building components using image-based scanning requires appropriate segmentation of the objects in the 2D building images.

papers.title: Shift-Aware Identity-Guided Latent Refinement for Referring Audio--Visual Segmentation
papers.abstract: Referring Audio--Visual Segmentation (Ref-AVS) is an emergent multimodal task requiring the precise identification and segmentation of a specific object based on a natural language expression grounded in both visual and auditory cues.

papers.title: Representation Alignment from a Few Paired Data via Distilled Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: Aligning two independently pretrained unimodal encoders typically demands millions of paired examples. In this paper, we study the regime where only $N \sim 100$--$500$ pairs are available, while unpaired data on either side is abundant.

papers.title: Coordinate-Free Automatic Differentiation
papers.abstract: Automatic differentiation (AD) is a cornerstone of modern machine learning. Since all AD frameworks implicitly fix a basis of Euclidean space to define gradients and Jacobians, they natively process mathematical objects that are arrays of a fixed set of coordinates.

papers.title: Credit Attribution in Timestamped Soccer Networks Using Multivariate Hawkes Processes
papers.abstract: The two main traditional player statistics used in soccer are goals scored and assists, with an assist credited when a player's pass immediately leads to a teammate scoring.

papers.title: REDaCT: Collapse-Free Unlearning in Large Reasoning Models
papers.abstract: Unlearning in large reasoning models (LRMs) requires removing forget-set information from both the reasoning trace and the final answer.

papers.title: Semantic Views: Certified Reuse of LLM Labels Across Semantic Queries
papers.abstract: Semantic query engines evaluate natural-language filters with a large language model, and every evaluation is a costly oracle call.

papers.title: Faithful and Complete LLM-Assisted Automated Construction of Hierarchical Hardware Knowledge Graphs
papers.abstract: Hardware datasheets contain engineering specifications essential for component selection, system integration, and hardware compatibility verification.

papers.title: DistressBench: Evaluating Multi-Dimensional Crisis Support in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Language models have been adopted faster than evaluation practices that reliably assess their risks, and a growing share of use is affective rather than informational. Within that traffic users disclose suicide and self-harm (SSH) crises.

papers.title: MADS: Multi-Agent Dialog Simulation for Robust Conversational Agents
papers.abstract: Task-oriented conversational agents remain fragile under realistic conditions, especially when users exhibit non-cooperative behavior. Existing function-calling benchmarks underrepresent adversarial conversation trajectories, thereby limiting the training resources available for developing robust agents.

papers.title: NV-Tesseract-AD: Curriculum-Enhanced Conditional Diffusion for Multivariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: We propose NV-Tesseract-AD, a curriculum learning-enhanced conditional diffusion framework for multivariate time-series anomaly detection.

papers.title: Trajectory Prediction for Autonomous Driving in Road Construction Zones Using Human-in-the-Loop Driving Data
papers.abstract: Ego-trajectory prediction in urban roadway work zones remains an underexplored topic in autonomous-driving research, with limited dedicated data and systematic evaluation.

papers.title: Static Gradient Attribution Underperforms a Density-Matched Random Mask on Loss-Based Forgetting Within LoRA B-Matrix
papers.abstract: Parameter-efficient continual learning updates a restricted subset of adapter parameters to incorporate sequential tasks while limiting catastrophic forgetting. Gradient attribution is a common rule for selecting that subset, but it requires an additional backward pass over calibration data.

papers.title: Neural expectation-maximization and meta-models
papers.abstract: We interpret Transformer networks as learned approximations to a hybrid probabilistic-inference procedure that combines max-product Loopy Belief Propagation (LBP) with Expectation--Maximization (EM).

papers.title: Minimax Rates for Estimating Powered Sliced Wasserstein Functionals
papers.abstract: We study the two-sample estimation of the powered Sliced Wasserstein functional under projected $r$-th moment assumptions. Let $N=n\wedge m$, where $n$ and $m$ are two sample sizes. We establish the minimax rates in the noncritical regimes.

papers.title: KITE: A Knowledge-Injected Temporal Encoder for Time-Series Event Forecasting
papers.abstract: Forecasting rare, high-cost events in multivariate time-series systems is hard because their precursors are seldom observed, so a purely data-driven model has little to learn from. The engineers who run these systems, however, hold knowledge that precedes such events, information absent from the scarce labels.

papers.title: Kernelized Parameter Sensitivity Atlases for Amortized Conditional Interpretability
papers.abstract: Gradient-based attribution provides input-specific information about model parameters, but computing it via backpropagation for many samples is expensive, while static importance scores discard input dependence.

papers.title: Reference-Free Food Volume Estimation from Egocentric Stereo Video
papers.abstract: Current stereo vision-based approaches for food portion estimation are hindered by the user burden of using a mobile phone to capture multiple images or placing a reference object in the scene for scale calibration.

papers.title: StereoEngine: Scaling Stereo Bimanual Robot Data without Stereo Cameras
papers.abstract: Stereo vision is increasingly used for robotic manipulation, with a growing body of work incorporating it into Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. However, the scarcity of large-scale, real-world stereo datasets remains a fundamental bottleneck for scaling such policies.

papers.title: A Categorical Atlas of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning: Cones, Orbits, and Gauges
papers.abstract: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning has hundreds of methods, usually compared by parameter count and benchmark score. We compare them as maps. A pretrained checkpoint is a base point in weight space, and a weight-space method is a smooth map from a small parameter space that starts at that point.

papers.title: Zebra3D: Efficient Hybrid Foundation Models For Scalable 3D Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Feed-forward 3D foundation models reconstruct scenes from unposed images, but the quadratic cost of global attention limits their scalability to large view sets.

papers.title: Spatial Context or Memory? Sizing the Inputs of Neural Surrogates for Partially Observed Fields
papers.abstract: Neural surrogates that forecast a physical field from sparse, noisy sensors read a window of nearby sensors and a history of past snapshots. Practitioners choose both by comparing fitted models with each other. Such comparisons cannot tell a model's shortfall from missing information.

papers.title: A Distributional Framework for Behavioral Characterization and Risk Management of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models are stochastic by nature. Repeated executions under the same experimental conditions may produce different responses. We propose a framework that can be applied across the model lifecycle, from task design to residual behavior and continuous monitoring.

papers.title: Byzantine-Resilient Federated Large Language Model via Hypergraph Message Passing
papers.abstract: Federated Large Language Models (FedLLMs) are promising to deliver privacy-preserving, collaborative intelligence. The decentralized training process is vulnerable to Byzantine attacks that corrupt semantic consistency and factual resilience through malicious model updates.

papers.title: Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling
papers.abstract: Vision-language reward models are trained on annotated preference pairs, which are expensive to collect, can disagree, and are ranked by benchmark accuracy.

papers.title: PVBRF-ID: Private, Verifiable and Byzantine-Robust Federated Intrusion Detection for Oilfield Enterprise Networks
papers.abstract: Federated learning allows dispersed oilfield sites to train a shared intrusion detector without pooling network traffic, yet its aggregation step forces a choice between privacy and robustness.

papers.title: Bridging Human and Model Attention: Explainability Analysis of CNN, Mamba, and ViT Architectures with Gaze-Based Validation
papers.abstract: High-risk applications of deep learning require precise characterization of model decision-making. We conduct a systematic explainability evaluation across Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Vision Transformers (ViTs), and Vision Mamba (ViM).

papers.title: Product Monte Carlo: Expectation Under a Product of Densities
papers.abstract: Aggregating independently computed sub-sample inferences is a well-known challenge in large-scale Bayesian computation, federated learning, and opinion pooling. The core problem is to approximate a distribution whose density is proportional to a product of individual densities.

papers.title: Activating the Annotator: Operationalising Lived Experience in Data Annotation
papers.abstract: Perspectivist NLP has established that annotator positionality shapes labels for subjective tasks, but the field still lacks methods for operationalising it.

papers.title: Primal-Dual Flow Matching for Sample-Wise Constrained Generation
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of learning to generate data while satisfying a prescribed \emph{sample-wise} constraint with a user-specified probability of constraint satisfaction.

papers.title: Toward Maximizing Algebraic Connectivity via Density-Dependent Backbone Construction and Reinforcement Learning Completion
papers.abstract: This paper studies an open network design problem of constructing graph topologies with maximum algebraic connectivity under fixed numbers of vertices and edges.

papers.title: Critical Mass: Structure-Disjoint Splits Drift With the Libraries They Are Built On
